title: Sequence the kinematic problem-solving steps
instructions: Drag the steps into the order you would apply them to solve a uniform-acceleration problem. Click 'Check order' when ready.

events_timeline.label: Identify the known quantities (u, a, t, s, v) and the unknown
events_timeline.description: Pick the kinematic equation that involves your unknown.

events_timeline.label: Choose a positive direction and a starting point (origin)
events_timeline.description: Establish a frame of reference for signs.

events_timeline.label: Write Newton's-style sign conventions for u, a
events_timeline.description: Up = +, so for free fall a = -g.

events_timeline.label: Substitute into the chosen kinematic equation
events_timeline.description: v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², or v² = u² + 2as.

events_timeline.label: Solve for the unknown algebraically
events_timeline.description: Watch the units to make sure they're consistent.

events_timeline.label: Sanity-check the answer (sign, magnitude, units)
events_timeline.description: Does the value make physical sense? Did you use displacement (not distance)?
